name: BROWNFIELD (MATTHEW & KRISTIN)
address: 3126 NW QUIET RIVER LN, BEND, OR 97701

fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Open Lawn Area; Dense Vegetation; Water Feature; Walkway; Landscaped Area
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Water Feature; Limited Rear Access
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance to help responders confirm the correct property from the road.
• Mark the single driveway entrance clearly so responders can identify it quickly on arrival.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges to keep the path clear for emergency vehicles.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the residence to maintain a clear path around the structure for responders on foot.
• Keep a clear walking path between the front driveway and the rear of the property so responders can reach all sides of the home.
• Mark the location of the water feature so arriving responders can avoid it in low-light or fast-moving situations.
• Install a physical barrier or visible edging along the water feature to prevent responders from stepping into it during nighttime or smoke-obscured operations.
• Identify and mark any secondary foot access to the rear of the property, even if vehicle access is not possible.
• Keep the walkway clear of decorative objects, planters, or landscaping that could block or slow responder movement to the front entrance.
• Thin dense vegetation that could slow responder movement around the sides of the home.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Mixed Vegetation; Vegetation Near Structure; Water Feature; Limited Vegetation Separation; Woody Debris; Vegetation Along Driveway; Large Trees; Open Terrain
wildfire.recommendations:
• Trim back all shrubs and plants growing directly against the house walls on all sides.
• Remove woody debris, brush piles, and fallen branches from around the house and any outbuildings.
• Thin the tree clusters near the structure to increase open space between individual trees and the building.
• Remove low-hanging branches from large trees closest to the house.
• Cut back the mixed shrubs and plants surrounding the structure to create wider open gaps between vegetation and the walls.
• Clear overhanging branches and shrubs along both sides of the driveway to keep it passable for vehicles.
• Remove or cut back vegetation growing along the driveway edges that has grown into the travel lane.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure so their canopies do not touch or overlap each other close to the building.
• Remove dead branches, leaf litter, and dry plant material from the ground around the base of the tree clusters near the house.
• Keep the area immediately surrounding the house as clear as possible of plants, debris, and dead material.
• Clear any dead plant material or debris that has collected near the water feature if it is adjacent to the structure.
• Maintain open ground between the scattered trees and the house by removing low vegetation growing beneath them.
